methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents distributed capacity-building outside the NoVA corridor, signaling peer-to-peer learning infrastructure that could democratize deep AI fluency beyond traditional tech hubs if scaled regionally.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - wtkr.com
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops by a Norfolk native directly address the technology gap through community-driven education, exemplifying grassroots distributed learning that builds foundational fluency rather than passive platform consumption.

signals.title: After severe 76% electricity price hikes due to AI data centers, Virginia requires firms to pay for all dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure — state regulators crack down, governor says move will save civilians ‘hundreds of millions of dollars’ - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: 76% electricity price hikes from data centers impose concentrated infrastructure costs on distributed populations who gain no AI capability benefits—a perfect storm of concentrated extraction and shallow civilian engagement with the underlying technology.

signals.title: Column: For rural Virginia, data centers are more than technology - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: The column's framing of data centers as economic opportunity 'for rural Virginia' reveals the infrastructure/capability disconnect—physical presence of AI infrastructure doesn't translate to distributed deep skills, reinforcing metro concentration of actual technological expertise.

signals.title: AI in Roanoke County schools: How new policies will guide student use - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: School AI policies in Roanoke County focus on student usage guidelines rather than computational literacy development, signaling shallow platform adoption where students consume AI tools without building underlying technical understanding or agency.
